title: Hindbrain, midbrain and forebrain
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Hindbrain, midbrain and forebrain
card: The lowest part of the brain, next to the spinal cord. It runs functions needed to stay alive, such as breathing and heart rate, and it helps control balance.
The small middle part. It relays sensory and movement information between the hindbrain and the forebrain.
The largest and highest part. It handles complex thought, such as planning, reasoning and language.
The three parts work together. A single task, such as catching a ball, uses all of them.
draft.remember: Hindbrain keeps you alive and balanced, midbrain relays information, forebrain does the complex thinking.

a.q: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for planning and reasoning?
a.why: The forebrain handles complex thought such as planning and reasoning. The midbrain is a tempting choice because it sits in the middle, but its job is to relay sensory and movement information.
a.clue: Think about which part handles complex thought.

b.q: After an accident, Liam can think and speak clearly, but he needs a machine to help him keep breathing. Which part of his brain is most likely damaged?
b.why: Breathing is a survival function run by the hindbrain. Liam's clear thinking and speech suggest his forebrain is working. The midbrain is tempting, but it relays sensory and movement information rather than running breathing.
b.clue: Which part runs the functions needed to stay alive?
